card.name: Zinli
card.tagline: Fon funeral drum-dance of the Abomey plateau
card.profile: Zinli (formerly Avi-Zinli) is a Fon funeral rhythm and dance from the Abomey plateau of Benin, created in the 19th century by Prince Gbinyin — the future King Glèlè (reigned 1858–1889) — for the funeral of a friend of his father, King Guézo (Numeridanse; CID). It is danced with lightness and flexibility to the zin (a vase-shaped drum that gives the rhythm its name), supported by gongs, rattles, hand-claps and song; an academic study notes a distinctive 24/8 metric structure with instruments including the kpezinga, kpezinvi and gan bells.
card.insight: Long reserved for funerary use, zinli was popularized from the 1980s by the artist Alèkpéhanhou (Michel Loukou), "the king of renewed Zinli," carrying a sacred Dahomean court tradition to wide popular and international audiences while remaining an intangible cultural marker of Abomey identity (Numeridanse; academic study).
